newsitem.title: USA: No muni work in Azle, Texas, for awhile - Rauscher.
newsitem.headline: No muni work in Azle, Texas, for awhile - Rauscher.

text.p: Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc will not be doing negotiated bond underwriting for the town of Azle, Texas, any time soon because of a $150 contribution by an employee before that employee came on board at the firm, a company official said Thursday.

The situation, outlined by Rauscher in a quarterly report to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, highlights one of the trickiest provisions of the board's "pay-to-play" rule G-37, which was enacted in April 1994.
Rule G-37 bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing negotiated bond business for two years with those governments.
The ban on business applies even to those employees that made contributions before they were hired.
For example, if a person was hired six months after making a contribution, then the dealer is barred from doing business with that issuer for another 18 months, the MSRB says.
Rauscher said in its quarterly filing that a member of its municipals staff contributed $150 in May 1996 to Leck Heflin, a candidate for Azle's city council.
The staff member "did not begin working for our firm until Oct 21," Rauscher said in its filing.
"They sure can't do business with that city council," Christopher Taylor, executive director of MSRB, said in a telephone interview.

He said the purpose of the so-called "lookback provision" in G-37 is to make sure firms "don't go out and hire somebody that has made a (lot) of contributions and then get all the business" from the recipients of the gifts.
Dyer Greer, a compliance officer in Rauscher's Dallas office, said, "This is the first contribution we've ever had to report."
"I go through and ask everbody subject to the rule, 'Did you make any contributions this quarter?' That's how I discovered it," Greer said in a telephone interview.
"We think we did everything to the letter. We reported it as we interpreted the law," Greer said.
He said a curb on negotiated bond business with Azle, which sits 15 miles northwest of Fort Worth and has a population of only 10,000, should not put much of a dent in Rauscher's activities.
Rauscher ranked 14th among the top 50 managers of negotiated bond deals in 1995, according to Securities Data Co.
